newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kind words for Britain's Blair from Mandela.
newsitem.headline: Kind words for Britain's Blair from Mandela.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela on Friday claimed British Labour Party leader Tony Blair as a friend, but stopped short of endorsing him as Britain's next prime minister.
"I know that an election is coming (in Britain) and I will not interfere, but these are our friends and I wish them well," Mandela told reporters after meeting Blair in Cape Town.
Blair, widely tipped to defeat Conservative Party Prime Minister John Major in Britain's next general election, was in the city for a Commonwealth Press Union meeting starting on Sunday.
Posing with Mandela for pictures, Blair said his Labour Party supported changes in South Africa and the struggle to make the country an economic success.
"We will do everything we can both in opposition and if elected in government to help further the course of progress here and develop South Africa," Blair said.
He denied that his visit was a public relations exercise meant to upstage British Prime Minister John Major's speech at the Conservative Party congress in Bournemouth.
"This visit is important between our two countries...there are reasons of history, politics and commerce why our two countries should develop close and strong ties," Blair said.
Mandela paid tribute to Britain's Labour Party for the support it gave to his African National Congress during the fight against apartheid.
"I express to him my sincere thanks for the support we got from the Labour Party and to do so is not to interfere in the domestic affairs of Britain," he said.
